questions.stem: Which of the following correctly distinguishes quality control from quality assurance?
options: Control inspects at the end; assurance builds quality in at every stage
Assurance inspects at the end; control builds quality in
They are two words for the same process
Control applies to services and assurance to manufacturing
questions.why: Control finds defects after they have been made, so the materials and labour in them are wasted. Assurance prevents them, which is cheaper.
whyNot: This reverses the two.
They are distinct, and it is the distinction examiners test most.
Both apply to either sector.

questions.stem: Which term is defined as: a small group of employees who meet regularly to identify and solve quality problems in their own area?
options: Quality circle
Total Quality Management
Kaizen
Quality control
questions.why: Quality circles work because the people doing the job know where the problems are, and being asked is motivating. They fail when suggestions are ignored.
whyNot: TQM is the whole-organisation approach to quality.
Kaizen is continuous improvement through many small changes.
Quality control is end-of-process inspection.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of Kaizen?
options: Continuous improvement through many small changes, largely suggested by employees
A single large transformational improvement project
Inspecting products at the end of production
Holding minimal inventory
questions.why: Kaizen is incremental, cheap and low-risk, and the gains compound. Its weakness is that it cannot deliver a step change when one is needed.
whyNot: Kaizen is the opposite: many small changes rather than one big one.
That is quality control.
That is just in time.

questions.stem: What is the central idea of Total Quality Management?
options: Every employee is responsible for quality, treating the next stage as their customer
A specialist department checks all output
Only managers are responsible for quality
Quality is checked by the customer after purchase
questions.why: The internal customer idea is what makes TQM work: if everyone meets the requirements of the next stage, the external customer receives something correct by construction.
whyNot: That is quality control, which TQM replaces.
TQM spreads responsibility to everyone, not just managers.
That would be leaving quality to chance.

questions.stem: Why is quality control impossible for a guesthouse stay?
options: You cannot inspect a guest's stay after it has happened and replace the defective one
Guesthouses have no quality standards
Guests do not notice quality
Quality control is illegal in tourism
questions.why: Services are consumed as they are delivered, so there is no finished product to inspect before the customer receives it. The standard has to be built into how every room is prepared and every guest greeted, which is quality assurance.
whyNot: They are judged publicly against standards through review scores.
Reviews show guests notice in considerable detail.
There is no such restriction.

questions.stem: What is the main drawback of Total Quality Management?
options: It is a cultural change that takes years and needs visible management commitment
It increases the number of defects
It removes responsibility from employees
It can only be used in manufacturing
questions.why: TQM is not a procedure to install. Introduced half-heartedly it becomes a slogan staff rightly ignore, and some businesses have spent heavily for very little.
whyNot: Its purpose and usual effect is to reduce defects sharply.
It gives every employee responsibility for quality.
It is widely used in services.

questions.stem: Which chain best links quality to competitive advantage?
options: Better quality reduces waste and rework, and raises satisfaction and repeat purchase, so profit rises through both cost and revenue
Better quality raises costs, so profit falls
Better quality has no financial effect
Better quality only affects the marketing budget
questions.why: Running the chain through both cost and revenue is stronger than running it through one. Fewer defects cuts cost; better reviews and repeat purchase raise revenue.
whyNot: Quality does cost money to build in, and the comparison with the cost of poor quality is the point.
It affects waste, returns, reputation and repeat purchase directly.
It affects operations, costs and revenue, not just promotion.

questions.stem: Why is over-engineering a budget product a form of waste?
options: The customer is not willing to pay for quality beyond what the market expects
Higher quality always reduces sales
Budget products cannot be made well
Quality standards are illegal for budget products
questions.why: Quality means meeting customer requirements, not maximising specification. Cost added that customers will not pay for is waste, and saying so shows genuine understanding of what quality means.
whyNot: Higher quality usually supports sales; the issue is cost the customer will not fund.
They can be made to an appropriate standard, which is the point.
No such restriction exists.

questions.stem: Why do quality circles sometimes fail?
options: Management asks for suggestions and then ignores them
Employees never have any ideas
They are too expensive to run
They require specialist consultants
questions.why: Genuine involvement motivates; consultation that changes nothing is worse than never asking, because it signals that staff views do not matter. Same point as consultation in WBS11 topic 1.3.4.4.
whyNot: The people doing the job usually know exactly where the problems are.
They are among the cheapest quality initiatives.
They are run by the employees themselves.
